lines: Baker, Isaiah 55 is the LORD throwing the doors wide open and calling, COME. Thirsty? Come. No money? Come anyway. What He offers is free (Isa 55:1).

And what He offers is the thing that actually satisfies. People keep spending money and work on what doesn't (Isa 55:2). That's paying for a gym membership every month and only ever using the parking lot.
The real feast is listening to Him. The LORD says, "listen, so that your soul may live." Then He backs it with an everlasting covenant, His loving devotion promised to David (Isa 55:3).

And this invitation doesn't stay small. He made David a witness to the nations, and nations who don't know the people He's inviting will RUN to them, because the LORD has bestowed glory on them (Isa 55:4-5). The guest list just went WORLDWIDE.

So answer while the door's open: "Seek the LORD while He may be found;" let the wicked man forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts and return to the LORD, and He will freely pardon (Isa 55:6-7). FREELY. Same price tag as the water!

Sound too good to be true? Not for Him. His thoughts and ways are higher than ours, as high as the heavens over the earth (Isa 55:8-9), and His word never comes back empty. Like rain and snow, it does what He sends it to do (Isa 55:10-11). I send one message to a group chat and get back... NOTHING. His word? Never.

It all ends in joy and peace, with singing mountains, clapping trees and cypress where the thornbush was, a name for the LORD that lasts forever (Isa 55:12-13). That's the whole chapter, friend: the LORD Himself is what satisfies, it costs you nothing, and the call reaches all the way to the nations. So come thirsty, come broke, just COME.
